what_its_for: Entecavir is an antiviral medicine used to treat chronic (long-term) hepatitis B infection in adults and children. Hepatitis B is a virus that attacks the liver. This medicine helps lower the amount of hepatitis B virus in your body, which helps protect your liver from damage.
how_to_take: Take entecavir by mouth, either as a tablet or as a liquid (oral solution). Take it on an EMPTY STOMACH — at least 2 hours before eating or 2 hours after eating. Taking it with food can make it work less well. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. If you are using the liquid, use the measuring spoon provided — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual dose for adults and teenagers (16 years and older) is 0.5 mg once daily. If you have had previous hepatitis B treatment that stopped working (called treatment-experienced), your doctor may prescribe 1 mg once daily. For children under 16, the dose is based on body weight and will be determined by your doctor. Always follow the exact dose your doctor has prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if it is still the same day you were supposed to take it. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep them in the original container, away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store in the bathroom. Store the liquid (oral solution) at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Do not freeze the liquid. Keep all medicines out of the reach of children. Throw away any unused liquid after the expiration date on the bottle.
what_to_avoid: Do not stop taking entecavir without talking to your doctor first — stopping suddenly can cause your hepatitis B to come back worse than before and can seriously harm your liver. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can cause additional liver damage. Do not share needles, syringes, or personal items like razors or toothbrushes, as hepatitis B can spread to others. Use barrier protection (such as condoms) during sex to protect your partner. Entecavir does NOT prevent spreading hepatitis B to others.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice any of the following: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice); dark-colored urine or pale-colored stools; severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting; unusual muscle pain or weakness; trouble breathing or feeling very cold; dizziness or lightheadedness; fast or irregular heartbeat; feeling very tired or weak for no reason. These could be signs of serious side effects including lactic acidosis (a dangerous build-up of acid in the blood) or serious liver problems.
when_it_works: Entecavir starts working right away to fight the hepatitis B virus, but you may not feel any different because hepatitis B often has no symptoms. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to check that the medicine is working and to monitor your liver. It is very important to keep taking this medicine every day, even if you feel well. Treatment is usually long-term — do not stop unless your doctor tells you to.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. The risks and benefits will need to be discussed. There is a pregnancy registry to monitor outcomes if you take this medicine during pregnancy. BREASTFEEDING: It is not known if entecavir passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. KIDNEY PROBLEMS: If your kidneys do not work well, your doctor may lower your dose or have you take it less often. LIVER TRANSPLANT PATIENTS: Special dosing may be needed. HIV PATIENTS: Do not take entecavir to treat HIV infection — it is not approved for this and may cause HIV to become resistant to treatment. Make sure your doctor knows if you have HIV. ELDERLY: Older adults with kidney problems may need a dose adjustment.
